title: form
content_html:
form

The title found forms suggests that a form can be encountered before it is drawn or named. Alongside fluid forms, it raises the question of what makes a form recognisable when its outline, material or scale changes. Form can be something we recognise. To form can be something an artist, a material or a set of conditions does. The search for Plato’s Forms in we are the vessel gives this a personal stake. What are we looking for when we look for an ideal form? Found form (2017-07-09) · we are the vessel

Reading note. Existentialism and Mahāyāna Buddhism. Sartre uses a paper knife to illustrate how a manufactured object is made with an intended purpose. The Heart Sūtra speaks of form as empty. In the company of found forms, the readings raise two questions. What can we recognise before we know a thing’s purpose? What would it mean to see a form without giving it a fixed essence? Existentialism Is a Humanism · Heart Sūtra, §1.6
